# package controller

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-profinet/controller"
```

Package controller implements a PROFINET IO-Controller (conformance class A, RT\_CLASS\_1/2): it finds its devices by station name with DCP, optionally assigns their IP address, establishes an application relationship with each, parameterizes it, exchanges cyclic IO data, acknowledges alarms, reads and writes records and re-establishes the AR after a failure.

Each device runs its own lifecycle on its own goroutine; a failure of one does not affect the others. Process data is exchanged through [Device.SetOutput](#func-device-setoutput) and [Device.Input](#func-device-input).

#### func (Controller) CheckTopology

```go

```

CheckTopology finds the stations of the expected topology with DCP, reads the port data of each (PDRealData, with an implicit read: no AR needed) and compares the neighbors their LLDP reports with the expected links. It needs nothing written to the devices beforehand; PeerCheck is the way to have the devices watch their neighbors themselves.


RedundancyAck returns the redundancy acknowledge of the device's last input frame (DataStatus & rt.RedundancyMask, with the Redundancy bit): rt.PrimaryAck on the primary AR, rt.BackupAckWithData or rt.BackupAckWithoutData on a backup. ok is false before any frame.

#### func (Device) Reparameterize

```go
func (d *Device) Reparameterize(ctx context.Context, params []Parameter) error
```

Reparameterize writes parameters to the device while its AR runs: a PrmBegin, the writes, a PrmEnd, then it waits for the device's ApplicationReady (bounded by DeviceConfig.ActivityTimeout). Cyclic data goes on throughout; a device stops sending alarms until its ApplicationReady is acknowledged. The parameters also replace those of the same slot, subslot and index in the device's configuration, so that a reconnect writes them again. Only one re-parameterization of a device runs at a time.

It returns profinet.ErrInvalidState unless the device is running. A PrmBegin refused for the device's state (it is completing the ApplicationReady of its startup) is sent again for up to a second. When a step fails the AR is left as the device keeps it (a device that refused PrmBegin still runs with its old parameters); a device that sends no ApplicationReady makes it fail with profinet.ErrTimeout and aborts the AR (profinet.ErrAborted when the AR ends first), which then reconnects.

### type DeviceConfig

```go
type DeviceConfig struct {
	// StationName is the device's NameOfStation; required.
	StationName string
	// Model is the expected configuration; required. Its identity's vendor
	// and device ID must match what the device reports in DCP.
	Model *model.Device
	// IP is the IP suite the device should have. When AssignIP is true
	// and the device reports a different one, it is set with DCP
	// (temporarily, or permanently with PermanentIP). Without AssignIP the
	// device's own address is used.
	IP          dcp.IPSuite
	AssignIP    bool
	PermanentIP bool
	// SendClockFactor (units of 31.25 µs) and ReductionRatio define the
	// cycle; zero means 32 (1 ms) and 4: a cycle of 4 ms.
	SendClockFactor, ReductionRatio uint16
	// DataHoldFactor and WatchdogFactor are in cycles; zero means 10.
	// PLCs commonly use 3, which a general-purpose operating system does
	// not hold: its scheduling stalls of 10 to 20 ms expire a hold of 3
	// cycles of 4 ms (see docs/CYCLIC.md).
	DataHoldFactor, WatchdogFactor uint16
	// Advanced selects the advanced startup mode with RTClass 2;
	// otherwise the legacy startup with RTClass 1 is used.
	Advanced bool
	// RTClass states the RT class of the IOCRs; zero means the class of
	// the startup mode (RTClass2 with Advanced, RTClass1 without).
	// AddDevice refuses any other class with profinet.ErrUnsupported:
	// the controller has a data path for RT_CLASS_1/2 on Ethernet only,
	// not for RT_CLASS_UDP, RT_CLASS_3 or RT_CLASS_STREAM.
	RTClass pnio.RTClass
	// ActivityTimeout is the CM initiator activity timeout; zero means
	// 10 s.
	ActivityTimeout time.Duration
	// RTATimeoutFactor (units of 100 ms) and RTARetries configure the
	// alarm transport; zero means 5 and 3.
	RTATimeoutFactor, RTARetries uint16
	// Parameters are written after Connect and before PrmEnd.
	Parameters []Parameter
	// PeerChecks are the expected neighbors of the device's ports; they
	// are written (PDPortDataCheck) before Parameters, and the device
	// reports a remote mismatch diagnosis while a port's neighbor differs.
	PeerChecks []PeerCheck
	// MRP gives the device a media redundancy role (MRP records written
	// after the peer checks, before Parameters); nil writes none.
	MRP *MRPSetting
	// SystemRedundancy makes the AR an IOCARSR of an S2 AR set:
	// EXPERIMENTAL, not interoperable (sr.go).
	SystemRedundancy *SRSetting
	// RPCTimeout bounds each RPC call; zero means 5 s.
	RPCTimeout time.Duration
	// ReconnectMin and ReconnectMax bound the backoff between attempts;
	// zero means 200 ms and 10 s. ReconnectJitter (0 to 1) shortens each
	// wait randomly by up to that fraction, so that devices that failed
	// together do not reconnect together; zero waits exactly.
	ReconnectMin, ReconnectMax time.Duration
	ReconnectJitter            float64
	// OnAlarm receives every alarm, on the alarm goroutine of the AR; it
	// must not block.
	OnAlarm func(AlarmEvent)
	// OnState receives every state change, before WaitState returns for it.
	OnState func(from, to State, err error)
}
```

DeviceConfig configures a device of the controller.

### type PeerCheck

```go
type PeerCheck struct {
	// Subslot is the port submodule; zero means the first port, 0x8001.
	Subslot uint16 `json:"subslot,omitempty"`
	// Station is the expected neighbor's name of station and Port its
	// port, "port-001" for the first.

}
```

PeerCheck is an expected neighbor of one of a device's ports. The controller writes it to the port (PDPortDataCheck with CheckPeers) before PrmEnd; the device then reports a "remote mismatch" diagnosis, with an alarm, whenever the neighbor its LLDP sees is another one or none.

### type SRSetting

```go
type SRSetting struct {
	Discriminator [6]byte `json:"discriminator"`
	ConfigID      [8]byte `json:"configId"`
	// ARNumber is 1 or 2.
	ARNumber uint8 `json:"arNumber"`
	// Primary is the initial request.
	Primary bool `json:"primary"`
	// RedundancyDataHoldFactor is the SRInfoBlock's (the device's wait
	// for a primary, × 1 ms on go-profinet devices); zero means 200.
	RedundancyDataHoldFactor uint16 `json:"redundancyDataHoldFactor,omitempty"`
	// InputValidOnBackup asks for valid inputs on the backup AR.
	InputValidOnBackup bool `json:"inputValidOnBackup,omitempty"`
}
```

SRSetting makes the device's AR an IOCARSR of an S2 AR set: EXPERIMENTAL and not interoperable (see the device package's sr.go). The two controllers of a redundant pair give the device the same Discriminator and ConfigID and AR numbers 1 and 2; each says with its outputs whether its AR is to be primary (DataStatus "Primary Request") or backup ("Backup Request"), and Device.SetPrimary switches it.

### type State

```go
type State uint8
```

State is the state of a device's lifecycle on the controller.

```go
const (
	StateOffline State = iota
	StateResolving
	StateConnecting
	StateParameterizing
	StateWaitAppReady
	StateRunning
	StateStopped
)
```

States. A device goes Offline → Resolving → Connecting → Parameterizing → WaitApplicationReady → Running; a failure in any of them goes back to Offline (and after the backoff to Resolving); Close goes to Stopped.
